description:
MATERIAL. Every token is built from one primitive: the flat filled rectangle, drawn with no stroke and with partial opacity so overlaps read as lighter or darker patches. There are two populations of them. The first is a set of AXIS-ALIGNED HORIZONTAL BARS - planks, slats, ledger-rules - of widely varying length and thickness, stacked one above another around a shared vertical centre. The second is a much smaller set of LONG THIN ROTATED BATONS, sticks laid at angles of maybe 10-70 degrees, thrown across the stack and usually overrunning it at both ends. Nothing is curved, nothing is textured, there is no gradient, no outline, no type, no figure. The ground is a flat near-black warm charcoal in every tile.

WHAT IT IS A PICTURE OF. A STACK. Consistently and unmistakably: sawn timber cross-piled in a yard, a woodpile, a pallet of boards, and in the sparser seeds a cairn or a spine of stacked slabs with kindling flung over it. The diagonal batons read as loose sticks or a collapsed scaffold lying on top of the pile. A second, weaker reading is geological - horizontal strata, sediment bands, a core sample - and in the very thin seeds a ruled ledger with lines struck through it. It is architectural and material, not organic and not figurative.

WHAT THE TWELVE SHARE. All twelve are centre-weighted vertical accumulations of horizontal bars on the same black ground, in the same palette: a warm family of amber, ochre, caramel, tan and pale cream, set against a cool family of grey, taupe and dark umber. The saturated golds are the loudest thing in every tile and the greys do the settling. All twelve read portrait-ish in mass even though the tile is square, and all twelve place their weight on a single vertical axis with the widest and most saturated bars tending to the bottom or the very top.

HOW THEY DIFFER. Density is the main axis of variation. 1243682 and 1985692 are dense, fat, full-bleed slabs, almost solid; 1835793 is nearly empty, a scatter of hairline rules with four small gold bars in the middle and huge black margins; 1310661 is four detached heavy blocks with a real gap of black between the group and the bottom bar. The second axis is how much the diagonals intervene. 1283437 is DOMINATED by them - a small thin stack under a wide X of long sticks that reach nearly corner to corner - while 1310661 and 1985692 are almost purely horizontal. 1733538 is carried by one big pale cream diagonal slab that is the brightest thing on the sheet. The third axis is colour balance: 1310661, 1561509 and 1985692 sit in gold and brown; 1366079 and 1991107 lean grey and neutral and read cooler and flatter; 1203347 and 1475115 are dominated by a large pale sand mass. Width varies too - 1475115 is a wide chunky block, 1835793 and 1283437 are narrow.

ACROSS THE THREE STATES. The same seed stays the same object; what moves is the COUNT, THICKNESS AND SEPARATION of the layers and the reach of the sticks. Reading the four states tokens: 1310661 neutral is four separated blocks with an obvious black gap; in stress those blocks pack tight into one contiguous mass with more bars and the gap closes; in recovery the gap reopens and thin pale slivers appear inside the mass. 1283437 neutral is thin and airy under its X; stress THICKENS the stack into a denser striped column while the sticks pull in; recovery flings the sticks out longer and wilder, past the bottom of the frame, over a finely striped core. 1243682 neutral is a many-layered fine stack; stress coarsens it into fewer, taller, greyer blocks - the top block goes grey and the whole tile gets muddier; recovery returns the many thin layers and adds a second long diagonal. 1203347 changes least: stress darkens and thickens the lower mass and fattens the main diagonal, recovery adds a litter of thin horizontal slats and dark grey shards at the bottom so it looks shed or shaken loose. So: STRESS = consolidation, fewer and chunkier and greyer; RECOVERY = re-lamination, many thin layers plus longer scattered sticks. It is a real, legible change and it is the same change in all four.

AT 120PX. The stack silhouette survives completely - it is the strongest thing about the work, and the twelve still read as twelve different objects at browse size: sparse vs solid, gapped vs contiguous, gold vs grey, X-crossed vs purely horizontal. What is lost is the fine layer count and the thinnest rules: 1835793 collapses to a small floating cluster with almost nothing around it, and 1366079's hairlines and 1991107's finest slats mostly disappear into the ground. The diagonals survive as faint pale threads rather than as objects. The state change is still readable at 120 but quieter - 1310661's closing gap and 1283437's thickening are the two I can still call from the thumbnail; 1203347 neutral and stress are close to each other there.

THINGS I NOTICE THAT MIGHT BE FAULTS. Bars run off the left and right tile edges in 1243682, 1985692, 1991107 and 1366079, and in the states sheet 1243682's stress row has its top block cut by the top edge of the tile - I cannot tell whether that bleed is intended cropping or a shape overrunning the viewBox. 1835793 is so sparse it looks like a different, weaker project than 1243682. The hairline rules are at the edge of visibility even at 256. Overlaps themselves read as deliberate translucency, not as collisions.

COMPOSITION. Centre-weighted and axial. The dominant element is normally the widest, most saturated gold bar, with the diagonal batons as a crossing secondary gesture; where there is no diagonal and no size contrast the tile flattens into an even field of stripes with no focus - 1366079 is that case, and 1991107 nearly is. Margins are inconsistent by design: some tiles bleed off both sides, others float in a lot of black.
